evidence: Caes. BG 3.1.6; Cic. Rep. 1.19 (Lewis & Short s.v. dīvidō)
terms.comment: The classical phrase: Caesar has it of a village divided in two by a river, Cicero of a people. In the kitchen, with a knife, in duās partēs secāre.
Apicius’s kitchen verb; post-classical (Lewis & Short). The finite dīmidiāre is very rare (Tertullian), though the participle dīmidiātus, halved, is common (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: Cut the boiled cabbage shoots in half.

phrases.latin: Pānem in duās partēs frange: dīmidium tibi, dīmidium frātrī.
phrases.english: Break the bread in half: half for you, half for your brother.

sources: Lewis & Short: divido · Lewis & Short: medio · Lewis & Short: dimidio
